{{Short description|Number which describes the structure of the set of squares in a given field}}
{{Confuse|Pythagoras's constant|Height of a field}}

In [[mathematics]], the '''Pythagoras number''' or '''reduced height''' of a [[field (mathematics)|field]] describes the structure of the set of squares in the field.  The Pythagoras number <math>p(K)</math> of a field <math>K</math> is the smallest positive [[integer]] <math>p</math> such that every sum of squares in <math>K</math> is a sum of <math>p</math> squares.

A ''[[Pythagorean field]]'' is a field with Pythagoras number 1: that is, every sum of squares is already a square.

==Examples==
* Every non-negative [[real number]] is a square, so <math>p(\R)=1</math>.
* For a [[finite field]] of odd [[characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]], not every element is a square, but all are the sum of two squares,{{sfnp|Lam|2005|p=36}} so <math>p=2</math>.
* By [[Lagrange's four-square theorem]], every positive [[rational number]] is a sum of four squares, and not all are sums of three squares, so <math>p(\Q)=4</math>.

== Properties ==
* Every positive integer occurs as the Pythagoras number of some [[formally real field]].{{sfnp|Lam|2005|p=398}}

* The Pythagoras number is related to the [[Stufe (algebra)|Stufe]] by <math>p(F)\leq s(F)+1</math>.{{sfnp|Rajwade|1993|p=44}} If <math>F</math> is not formally real then <math>s(F)\leq p(F)\leq s(F)+1</math>,{{sfnp|Rajwade|1993|p=228}} and both cases are possible: for <math>F=\C</math> we have <math>s=p=1</math>, whereas for <math>F=\mathbb{F}_5</math> we have <math>s=1</math>, <math>p=2</math>.{{sfnp|Rajwade|1993|p=261}}

* As a consequence, the Pythagoras number of a non-formally-real field is either a power of 2, or 1 more than a power of 2. All such cases occur: i.e., for each pair <math>(s,p)</math> of the form <math>(2^k,2^k)</math> or <math>(2^k,2^k+1)</math>, there exists a field <math>F</math> such that <math>(s(F),p(F)) = (s,p)</math>.{{sfnp|Lam|2005|p=396}} For example,
**[[quadratically closed field]]s and fields of characteristic 2 give <math>(s(F),p(F))=(1,1)</math>;
**for primes <math>p\equiv 1\!\!\!\!\pmod{4}</math>, <math>\mathbb{F}_p</math> and the [[p-adic number|''p''-adic field]] <math>\Q_p</math> give <math>(1,2)</math>;
**for primes <math>p\equiv 3\!\!\!\!\pmod{4}</math>, <math>\mathbb{F}_p</math> gives <math>(2,2)</math> and <math>\Q_p</math> gives <math>(2,3)</math>;
** <math>\Q_2</math> gives <math>(4,4)</math>, and 
** the [[algebraic function field|function field]] <math>\Q_2(t)</math> gives <math>(4,5)</math>.

* The Pythagoras number is related to the [[height of a field]] <math>F</math>: if <math>F</math> is formally real then <math>h(F)</math> is the smallest power of 2 which is not less than <math>p(F)</math>; if <math>F</math> is not formally real then <math>h(F)=2s(F)</math>.{{sfnp|Lam|2005|p=395}}
